title: Procurement Planning and Bid Management
overview: Effective procurement planning is essential for ensuring supply security while balancing the goals of cost savings and internal customer satisfaction. This course covers comprehensive strategies for procurement planning and bid management, offering insights on setting procurement objectives, forecasting demand, and integrating vendors to sustain operations. Participants will explore both qualitative and quantitative forecasting techniques for inventory planning and learn to apply vendor management strategies that support the organization’s long-term goals.
audience: This course is designed for purchasing and supply chain professionals at all levels involved in procurement planning, sourcing, buying, and bid management, as well as those engaged in the purchasing process.
methodology: The course incorporates a mix of individual and team exercises, case studies, and instructional videos to enhance learning and practical application.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Develop strategic procurement objectives and initiatives aligned with long-term organizational goals
Categorize spend items to create targeted go-to-market strategies
Utilize forecasting techniques to improve procurement planning
Implement vendor integration strategies to maintain supply continuity
Apply scientific methods to evaluate and select vendor bids

items.text: Assessing financial impacts and vendor segmentation
Performing market risk and value chain analysis
Conducting SWOT analysis and Porter’s Five Forces
Using risk heat maps and vendor risk scoring
Exploring the human element of forecasting
Key insights from Tetlock’s “foxes and hedgehogs” and Taleb’s “black swan”
Applying quantitative and qualitative forecasting methods
Applying scoring systems and selection protocols
Awarding contracts based on Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for complex purchases
